summary: Describes the role and responsibilities of the Independent Submission Editor, who approves documents in the Independent Submission stream. The ISE is appointed by the IAB and works with draft editors, reviewers, the RFC Production Center and Publisher, and the RFC Series Editor.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8730 describes the role of the Independent Submission Editor, who manages the Independent Submission stream of RFCs. It explains how the editor is selected, what the editor does, and how volunteer reviewers support the work.

questions: what is the independent submission editor
subtitle: The responsibilities and qualifications of the editor who manages the Independent Submission stream.

tldr.problem: The Independent Submission stream needs a defined role for reviewing and managing submissions, aligned with the RFC Editor structure described in IASA 2.0.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the Independent Submission Editor's appointment, desired qualifications, responsibilities, support board, and funding context.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8730 obsoletes RFC 6548 and has been updated by RFC 9280 and RFC 9920.

today: RFC 8730 is Informational, obsoletes RFC 6548, and has been updated by RFC 9280 and RFC 9920.

sections.title: Purpose and Background
sections.content:
The RFC Editor Model defines streams that produce draft RFCs for publication. RFC 8730 describes the management function for the Independent Submission stream and the role of its Independent Submission Editor (ISE).

This document aligns the model with the IASA 2.0 structure, which created the IETF Administration LLC managed by a board of directors. It obsoletes RFC 6548, replacing references to earlier administrative structures.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 8730 defines the editor's role in the Independent Submission stream. It updates the earlier model to match the IASA 2.0 structure.

sections.title: The Independent Submission Editor
sections.content:
The ISE is one individual responsible for the Independent Submission stream. The stream and the ISE are not under the authority or direction of the RFC Series Editor or the RFC Series Oversight Committee. The ISE is appointed by and directly responsible to the Internet Architecture Board (IAB), after community input.

The RFC describes the position as senior. Desired qualifications include broad technical competence, familiarity with the RFC Series, skill in setting up review arrangements, standing in the technical community, editorial skill, command of English, and ability to work in an environment with divided responsibilities.
sections.plainLanguage: The ISE is one person who answers directly to the IAB. The role calls for technical knowledge, familiarity with RFCs, editorial skill, and the ability to coordinate work across groups.

sections.title: The Editor's Responsibilities
sections.content:
The ISE may have assistants and is responsible for seven areas of work. These include maintaining the stream's technical quality; reviewing, approving, and processing submissions; and forwarding draft RFCs to the RFC Production Center.

The ISE also develops the stream's scope, reviews and approves its RFC errata, coordinates work under general RFC Series policies, and provides statistics and documentation when requested by the RFC Series Editor or the LLC. The ISE may select an advisory board for special topics.

The IAB selects the ISE after collecting community input. The role is a volunteer function, while the IAB considers maintaining the stream a supported activity whose costs should be included in the IASA budget.
sections.plainLanguage: The ISE reviews submissions, maintains their technical quality, and sends approved drafts to the RFC Production Center. The ISE also handles errata, develops the stream's scope, and reports information when requested.

sections.title: The Editorial Board
sections.content:
The Independent Submission Editorial Board is a volunteer group that reviews documents in the stream. The board exists at the ISE's discretion, and its members serve at the ISE's discretion.

The RFC notes the board's existence but leaves further discussion of it outside the scope of this model. The ISE may also choose advisory-board members to help with special topics.
sections.plainLanguage: Volunteer editorial-board members review Independent Submission documents. The board and its membership serve at the ISE's discretion.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 8730 says it has no specific security implications. It directs readers to the security considerations in RFC 4846 and RFC 8729.
sections.plainLanguage: This document identifies no new security implications. It refers readers to the security considerations in RFC 4846 and RFC 8729.
